entities.evidence: אַבְרָם names Abram, the son of Terah later called Abraham. The source tag identifies the same bearer.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: כָּבֵד מְאֹד describes Abram as very wealthy, and the verse specifies his wealth in livestock, silver, and gold.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ introduces the personal name אַבְרָם, the subject of the clause.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: מְאֹד intensifies כָּבֵד, and the three following phrases specify what Abram had in abundance: livestock, silver, and gold.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used predicatively of Abram, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68622:11, 67347:2, 67347:3, 67346:3, 66565:8, 65823:8.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of degree, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Livestock, silver, and gold each take the preposition בְּ, specifying the respects in which Abram was כָּבֵד מְאֹד, “very wealthy.”
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ combines with the definite article, doubling the noun’s initial מ. The noun is masculine singular absolute and refers collectively to livestock.

analysis.evidence: כָּבֵד מְאֹד describes Abram as very wealthy. The three parallel phrases list his holdings in livestock, silver, and gold, so כֶּסֶף denotes silver held as wealth.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ incorporates the definite article, yielding בַּ and doubling the following כ. The noun is masculine singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: The repeated preposition ב marks livestock, silver, and gold as the possessions in which Abram was rich. The pairing of זָהָב with כֶּסֶף identifies gold as the metal.
analysis.morphology: וּ is the conjunction “and.” בַ is the preposition בְּ with the definite article, whose assimilation doubles the following ז. זָהָב is a masculine singular absolute noun.
